metadata.title: Hotel Lobby AI Video: Orange-Studio Duos & Prompts
metadata.description: Create an original Hotel Lobby-style AI video with two reference photos, an orange studio and hanging mic. Edit the prompt and review credits before generating.

generator.title: Create a Hotel Lobby-Style AI Video
generator.prompt: Create an original two-person performance using the two uploaded reference photos. Reference image 1 is the performer on the LEFT; reference image 2 is the performer on the RIGHT. Keep their faces, hairstyles, clothing and body proportions distinct. Place both performers in a seamless matte orange studio with one microphone hanging between them. Use a static, centered full-body shot with soft, even lighting. The left performer starts with small hand gestures while the right performer nods and reacts independently; then the right performer takes a turn while the left listens. Keep their feet planted, their positions fixed and a clear gap between their bodies. No side swaps, face blending, extra people, duplicated limbs, camera moves, cuts, text or logos. Create original movement rather than reproducing a specific artist or existing recording.

hero.title: Hotel Lobby AI: Your Duo, One Orange Studio
hero.description: Turn two reference photos into an original orange-studio duo with a hanging microphone and alternating performance. Start with the editable Hotel Lobby AI prompt below, choose available video settings, and make the scene your own.
hero.tip: Original scene generation. Exact source choreography, song reproduction and beat-matched lip sync are not guaranteed.

howTo.title: How to Make a Hotel Lobby AI Video
howTo.description: The generator starts in Image to Video with reference images and a scene prompt already selected. Review the settings before submitting a generation.

items.title: 1. Add two distinct references
items.description: Upload one clear photo per performer in the reference-image area. Use the first for the left character and the second for the right. Sharp faces, visible clothing and uncluttered backgrounds give the model clearer information.

items.title: 2. Edit the scene and settings
items.description: Adjust the prefilled prompt for your cast. Choose an available model, duration and aspect ratio. Start with a short clip to inspect the composition; use 16:9 for more space around both performers or 9:16 for a vertical composition.

items.title: 3. Review, generate and download
items.description: Check the displayed credit estimate, sign in and generate. Watch the entire result for identity changes, swapped positions and hands before downloading. Revise the prompt or photos if the first result needs another attempt.

introduce.title: What Is the Hotel Lobby AI Trend?
introduce.description: Hotel Lobby is the song title associated with Quavo and Takeoff's 2022 A COLORS SHOW performance. The AI trend reimagines its recognizable orange-studio duo format with new characters. It describes a creative format, rather than a separate AI model or a scene in an actual hotel.

items.title: One orange studio
items.description: A seamless orange wall and floor keep the focus on the performers. Ask for soft, even light, a hanging microphone and an uncluttered set instead of a hotel reception area.

items.title: Two separate identities
items.description: Assign each reference a fixed side in the prompt. Keep space between the characters and avoid crossing hands or overlapping bodies. Photo order is a prompt instruction; inspect the output because models can still swap or blend identities.

items.title: An alternating performance
items.description: Direct one performer to lead while the other reacts, then reverse the roles. Small independent gestures are easier to evaluate than synchronized dancing, large movements or rapid camera cuts.

ideas.title: Choose Your Duo
ideas.description: These are creative directions to try, not guaranteed output examples. Change the cast in the editable prompt while keeping the studio, positions and movement simple.

items.title: Friends or couples
items.description: Use two authorized photos and preserve each person's outfit. Give the left performer a brief opening gesture and the right performer a small reaction, then switch attention without changing positions.

items.title: Two pets
items.description: Describe each pet's fur markings, ears and size separately. Replace human hand gestures with subtle paw movements and head nods. Check for extra paws, duplicated tails or human facial features.

items.title: Original characters
items.description: Try two characters you designed or have permission to use. Describe their proportions and outfits clearly, and choose a consistent illustrated or realistic style for both references.

troubleshooting.title: Keep the Duo Recognizable
troubleshooting.description: Change one variable at a time when revising a result. A clear cast and restrained performance give you a more useful starting point than a long list of competing actions.

items.title: Faces blend or swap
items.description: Choose references with distinct outfits and clear faces. Repeat the left/right assignment, leave a visible gap between bodies and ask performers to stay on their own side. Review identity throughout the clip, not just in the first frame.

items.title: The scene loses its shape
items.description: Specify a seamless matte orange studio, one hanging microphone and a locked full-body camera. Remove furniture, extra props, pans and zooms from the prompt before adding complexity.

items.title: Hands or timing look wrong
items.description: Reduce gesture size, keep feet planted and ask for one performer to lead at a time. If both performers move identically, explicitly describe the other as listening and reacting independently.

faq.title: Hotel Lobby AI Questions
faq.description: Photos, sound, credits and what this workflow can do.

items.question: Is Hotel Lobby AI the same as the Migos AI video trend?
items.answer: These names commonly describe the orange-studio duo format associated with Quavo and Takeoff's Hotel Lobby performance. The scene is recognizable from its two performers and hanging microphone. You can read the Dreamina trend guide for another explanation of the format. Seadance Video is an independent platform and is not affiliated with the artists or COLORS.

items.question: How many photos should I upload?
items.answer: Start with two separate reference photos, one per performer. This page opens the reference-image workflow, which accepts two to three images for supported models. Two images keep the cast assignment simple. Use photos you have permission to animate and make each subject easy to identify.

items.question: Will my video reproduce the original movements exactly?
items.answer: This page creates a new performance from reference images and a text prompt. It is not a dedicated motion-transfer template for the original recording. Exact choreography, consistent identity and fixed left/right placement are not guaranteed. Video reference workflows are available in the general generator, but combining two character photos with a source performance is not provided by this page.

items.question: Does it include the original Hotel Lobby song?
items.answer: The page does not bundle the original song. A Generate Audio option may be available for your selected model; it generates audio rather than licensing or restoring the original recording. Exact lyrics and beat-matched lip sync are not guaranteed. If you add music later, use audio you have permission to use.

items.question: Can I make a Hotel Lobby AI video for free?
items.answer: You can read and edit the prompt without payment. Video generation requires signing in and enough credits for the selected settings. Review the estimate in the generator and see pricing and credits before submitting. This page does not promise a free video or unlimited attempts.

items.question: Which duration and format should I choose?
items.answer: Choose from the settings shown by your selected model. A short first clip helps you check the cast and composition before a longer attempt. Landscape 16:9 provides more room for two full-body performers; portrait 9:16 suits a vertical composition but needs careful spacing. Resolution and credit cost depend on the model and settings.

items.question: Can I use a single image of both performers?
items.answer: Yes, you can try a clear duo composition through the generator's first-frame image mode instead of reference images. A ready-made orange-studio image provides a starting layout, while separate references provide information about each character. Neither approach guarantees identity preservation; compare the complete result with your inputs.

items.question: Where can I learn more about the model and prompts?
items.answer: Visit the Seedance 2.0 generator page for supported workflows, the Seedance prompt guide for scene direction, or generation troubleshooting if a request fails. Available providers and controls are shown in the generator on this page.
